title: Using recycled R1 water for irrigation and firefighting
summary: On Sept. 30, 2026, a council member said reclaimed water use has fallen from about 5 million to about 3 million gallons a day since the fire, and that the County needs to build pipes to deliver it for irrigation. In March, the Kāʻanapali Resort R1 distribution system was 80 percent complete, with 200,000 to 300,000 gallons a day expected. In 2024 the council voted 9 to 0 to urge more R1 use to save drinking water for housing.

timeline.text: A council member said the County needs to build out pipes to deliver this reclaimed water.
The member said reclaimed water use fell from 5 million to about 3 million gallons a day after the fire.
The council voted 9 to 0 to adopt a resolution on using more R1 recycled water.
The chair said the resolution will move on.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: The committee voted seven ayes to recommend adoption of the amended resolution, with one member excused.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: One council member voted no in the roll call.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: Amendment to item number three of the revised resolution: The committee approved a change asking the administration to invest in R1 production at the Kahului, Molokaʻi and Lānaʻi plants.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: That change, with cultural uses added, passed eight to zero, with one member excused.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: A council member raised concern that the resolution did not specify affordable housing.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: The director said West Maui reuses about 50 percent.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: The environmental management director said South Maui reuses about 62 to 63 percent of its treated wastewater.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: The environmental management director said R1 water costs less than drinking water, but its price does not fully cover operating costs.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: The environmental management director offered to give another R1 presentation to the council and community if asked.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: The environmental management director said the next West Maui phase takes R1 water up to a county-owned reservoir at the 700-foot level.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: Another testifier said private users of R1 water should pay for its pipes and operations, with public uses served first.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: A testifier said she lost her home in the fire and called the item a priority.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: The Department of Water Supply director said the department strongly supports the item.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: The chair said drought and water shortages have put West Maui affordable housing projects in limbo.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: Resolution 24-161 urges the administration to make and deliver more recycled R1 water to save drinking water for housing.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

fromCommunityMeetings.who: a South Maui Community Plan Advisory Committee member
fromCommunityMeetings.quote: This basically just takes the treated water to the largest water user in the county so that they aren't using potable water for irrigation.
fromCommunityMeetings.about: Explains a proposed recycled water line from the Kīhei treatment plant to Wailea resorts so that irrigation would use reclaimed water instead of drinking water.

source.title: We Are South Maui: Community Plan Advisory Committee Meeting of March 8, 2023
